knowledgeEntries.why: the nigun breathes with the voice; a soft two-and-four arrives with the first chorus and sits on the felt pulse, not on the counted one. Kick on every beat is the simcha dance, not this form.
the freilach is a fast 2/4 danced in one-two: counted below about 110 the analysis has halved the pulse, above 190 it has doubled it. It is never rubato and never swung.
the maqsum's dum-tak cycle is the pulse; a mizrahi pop tune counted above about 145 is being counted in eighths. The darbuka pattern is syncopated, never a four-on-the-floor grid.
the produced pop ballad is a half-time backbeat: the snare lands on three of the felt bar. Above about 110 written BPM the count is the eighth-note, and the half-time reading is the arrangement.
one player and a voice: the strum is the pulse and it breathes. A four-on-the-floor kick under a fingerpicked song is a reading nobody in this world would give.

a rock band's backbeat is the written tempo across a wide band; above about 200 the count is the eighth-note and the band plays half-time. Four-on-the-floor is a real rock reading (disco-rock, motorik) and is not forbidden here.
the four-on-the-floor kick *is* the pulse and the genre is written at it. Counted below 100 the analysis has halved it (a 128 BPM track read as 64).
a standard is played at any tempo and the feel changes with it; above about 240 the band plays in two, which is still a swing feel and not a half-time backbeat. A jazz standard is never a dance grid.
a cue's pulse is the conductor's beat and it breathes; a written 180 is an ostinato counted in eighths over a felt 90. Score music is not built on a dance grid.
the 12/8 ballad is felt in four slow beats and the contemporary backbeat in four fast ones; both are the written tempo inside this band. The choir's tempo breathes, but the arrangement is not rubato.
the clave cycle is two written bars; a bossa notated in 2/4 counts around 130 and one notated in 4/4 counts around 65, so a count below 100 is the same music halved. Never a four-on-the-floor grid.

trap is written at 130-160 and felt at half of it (the snare on three of the felt bar); boom-bap is written at its own pulse near 90. Above about 110 the half-time reading is the one the producer means.

a ballad's pulse is slow. Above about 108 written BPM the analysis is counting the subdivision, not the pulse, and the arrangement is felt at half (the owner's song: 130.43 written, felt at 65). A ballad is never built on a dance grid.

produced pop sits on a backbeat at its written tempo; above about 135 the count is usually the eighth-note of a half-time chorus. Four-on-the-floor is a genuine pop reading (dance-pop) and stays available.

jazz.modeIsAPreference: `modeOnly: false` means the mode is not a *gate* here, not that the mode is unread. `approachToneChoice` looks inside the mode first for every style and falls back to any non-chord tone only when the mode offers nothing - which is what `allowOutOfMode` was always documented to mean. universalRule.claim: no style approaches a minor chord through its own major third - not the chord it sounds over, not the chord it leads to
universalRule.why: R-1b P1-6 names the note by the chord it sounds over ("E natural under Cm"): it sits a semitone from the minor third the keys hold for the whole beat it sounds, and resolving a beat later does not undo it. B-05c's harmony critic reads it the same way and grades it `major` whatever the style.
universalRule.foundOn: jazz-full, after B-18's own no-brief groove reading moved its bass: an E natural over Cm7 as a chromatic approach into the next chord's F. d5_roleFromFamilyLevel.claim: a family's own level chooses its role, not the section's energy (R-1b P1-2, the root remedy the stream's first two commits named and handed on)
d5_roleFromFamilyLevel.defect: B-18 replaced a global `-1 marking for the whole song` with per-family levels, so the owner's section markings rose a step (verses pp -> p, choruses mp -> mf). `sectionPhrasePlanner.assignRole` chose a family's role from `section.energy` - the *section's* intended level - so the strings, which the brief calls soft, were handed HARMONIC_BED instead of PAD in both middle choruses: the opposite of the brief. The anchor's track id became `strings-harmonic_bed` (a track takes the role of the first task that writes notes, and the Chorus is the first strings task), which is what broke five of B-05c's tests.

rule.statement: The section's own energy still sets the default - that is the arrangement's plan for the section, and it applies to every family the brief said nothing about. A family the brief *did* name is re-read at its own level (`familyLevelIn(arcSection, family)`), and the re-read is honoured only in the direction the brief asked for: a `support` family ("soft strings", "gentle bass", "light percussion") may only be given a *quieter* role than the section's default, never a busier one; a `feature` family ("big brass") may only be given a busier one.
rule.whyTheDirectionGate: A role boundary is not always a loudness boundary. Percussion at a low level takes FILL, whose ROLE_ACTIVITY is busier than the ACCENT it takes at a high one (rhythmic 0.6 vs 0.35, density 0.25 vs 0.20), so without the gate "light percussion" would have handed the percussion *more* notes in the two loud choruses than the section asked for. Busyness is `ROLE_ACTIVITY[role].density + ROLE_ACTIVITY[role].rhythmic`, because the two pairs this decides between differ on different axes.

namedConstants.PAD_CEILING_LEVEL: DYNAMIC_LEVEL.mp (0.4). A sustaining family holds one sonority at `mp` and under and moves with the harmony from `mf` up: a pad is what a string section plays when it is asked for weight without motion, and `mp` is the top of that range. This is the one threshold whose *boundary* moved: the old test was `section.energy < 0.4`, which put an exact `mp` on the bed side. Before B-18 the owner's choruses passed it only because a source prior nudged them to 0.398 - the pad was an accident of two thousandths, and it is now a stated rule. No benchmark-corpus section sits at exactly 0.4, so no golden case moved for it.
namedConstants.PERCUSSION_ACCENT_LEVEL: 0.6. Over this level a percussion part accents the arrangement rather than filling its gaps.
namedConstants.OSTINATO_RHYTHM_LEVEL: 0.6. The *measured* source rhythm over which comping runs as an ostinato (unchanged; named, not moved).

rule.dynamicShape: `dynamicShapeFor` moved inside the per-family loop and delegates to `arrangementArc.familyDynamicShape(arcSection, family)`, so each role assignment carries the marking its own family plays. The pre-arc delta fallback is unchanged.
rule.blastRadius: `familyEmphasisIn` is `neutral` for every family the brief did not name, and `familyDynamicShape` returns the section's own marking then, so an arrangement with no brief is byte-identical. All nine benchmark cases' section plans and composer digests are unchanged by this rule; the four golden cases that moved moved for the approach-tone preference in d3.

honestLimits: The plan side only, with one exception. No writer realises the intro figure, the ending gesture or the approach preference from the plan; the per-family *level* does now reach the writers, because the section planner writes each role assignment's `dynamicShape` from `familyDynamicShape(arcSection, family)` and the composer reads that string. The intro and ending intents are still plan-only.

`sectionPhrasePlanner` now reads the family's own level twice - `familyLevelIn` in `roleForFamily` and `familyDynamicShape` in `dynamicShapeFor`. What it still does not read is `familyEmphasisIn` anywhere but the direction gate: a `feature` family gets a busier role but no extra register, no extra entry, no doubling. "Big brass" moves one role and one marking, not an orchestration.

The family-word reader is adjacency-based on the producer's own text: an adjective reaches at most one word past the instrument, and a word about the world ends its reach. "Make the strings, which enter in the chorus, soft" is not read; it stays a global word.
`applyConstraint` ("not too busy", "less drums") is untouched: a *constraint* about a family is still compiled as a section-scoped density nudge, not as a family level.

The forbidden degrees are excluded whatever the target chord is. A minor-key song that genuinely borrows a major-III chord loses the major third as an approach tone into it; no case in the corpus does this, and no test covers it.

The style vocabularies judge an approach against the *key's* mode; B-05c's harmony critic judges it against the *chord's* own mode, and the two still disagree in principle. The strongest case (the major third of a minor chord) is refused in every style, and since this stream's fix a chromatic style prefers the key's mode where it can - which is what took jazz-full's two `approach_tone_wrong_mode` findings away and its harmony score to 96.4. The disagreement itself is unresolved: a genuinely out-of-mode approach that a chromatic style writes because the mode offers nothing admissible would still be graded `minor`, and no corpus case exercises that path today.

The five B-05c tests that failed with this stream on top of it are green, and four of them without touching the test. `critics/dimensions/ownerAnchor` 5/5, `critics/dimensions/harmony` 5/5, `critics/rank` 12/12. Two assertions were changed and both are recorded in `d5_roleFromFamilyLevel.testsChanged` with the measurement behind them: ownerAnchor's `toPerform.length === 1` (a knife-edge at the dimension's 0.12 on-grid boundary) and rank's `intro >= 12` (a count of blocking findings that fell from 13 to 10 because the arrangement improved). No threshold inside a dimension was moved and jazz-full was not added to `belowNinety`.
`tonalCentreOf` reads one tonal centre for the whole part window. A song that modulates is read in its opening key; the fixture does not modulate (keyChanges 0).

The pulse conventions are the B-18 specialist's generalisations about each style, not measurements of a corpus — the same standing as every other knowledge-base value. Their bands are round numbers a musician would defend, and each carries its why.

`inferStyleFromSong` claims a *form*, never a tradition: a triadic minor song with a slow harmonic rhythm and no rhythm section reads as ballad-shaped, and which world it belongs to stays a question. It returns `unknown` whenever the evidence supports no reading.

The no-brief reading replaces a bad default only: it is consulted when the map's answer is a reading the style forbids or a dance grid nothing evidenced. A defensible measurement is never overwritten (the eight corpus cases with a detected rhythm section keep their readings; only jazz-full changed, and only because its ii-V vocabulary forbids four_on_floor).

`groove.pulseStrategy` outranks `groove.family` in `grooveFromGrammar`. A knowledge entry whose pulse strategy and groove family disagree would now be read by the strategy; every shipped entry's pair agrees, and no test enforces the invariant across future entries.

The role rule is a one-step rule. `roleForFamily` compares two roles and takes one of them; it cannot express "two steps quieter", and a family the brief puts 2 markings under the section ("barely there") gets the same role as one put 1 under whenever both land in the same branch. The level itself does carry the difference into the `dynamicShape` and from there into the composer.

`PAD_CEILING_LEVEL` moved a boundary, not only a name: `section.energy < 0.4` became `level <= 0.4`, so a section whose intended level is exactly `mp` now puts a sustaining family on a pad. That is the musical statement (`mp` is the top of the pad range) and it is the reading the owner's song had before B-18 - but there it held by a source-prior nudge of two thousandths rather than by a rule. No benchmark-corpus section sits at exactly 0.4, so nothing in the golden corpus measures the change; the first arrangement that does will be the evidence.

jazz-full's harmony dimension is 96.4 here against 100 on `origin/main` f2119cb. The remaining 3.6 points are a `clash_share` minor on the bass in the Chorus (clashShare 0.0657 vs 0.034), left by B-18's no-brief groove reading writing a different bass line. It is above the `>= 90` gate, it is not hidden, and it is not fixed.

The owner's `single_voice_bed` is still 6 sections. This stream did not reduce it and does not claim to: R-1b P0-1's defect is downstream of the composer (the voices are written and lost in performance / repair), and the fix here makes the loss *larger* - 402 composed string notes shipping as 91 - and better localised, with 5 of the 6 sections now carrying the composed notes as evidence instead of 2.
